lesson.title: What Points on a Graph Really Mean
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: A proportional relationship graphs as a straight line through the origin. Today, learn to read real meaning out of any point on that line.

Every point (x, y) on a proportional relationship's graph tells a real story about the situation. If y = 4x represents the total cost (y) of buying x notebooks at $4 each, then the point (3, 12) means: buying 3 notebooks costs $12. The point (1, 4) is special — it's always the unit rate itself, showing the cost of exactly one item. Graph the line y = 4x on paper (or describe 3 points on it) and explain in words what each point means in the notebook-cost context.
You just translated abstract graph points into real, meaningful sentences. Tomorrow we'll use proportional reasoning to solve real percent problems.

objectives: Interpret a point (x, y) on a proportional relationship's graph in terms of the real-world context
Identify the point (1, k) as representing the unit rate
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's equation y=4x.
2. Graph or describe the line, plotting a few points together.
3. Translate each point into a real sentence about notebooks and cost.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: real-world percent problems.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one point (3,12) and its meaning before generalizing to others
Ready for more: ask them what the point (0,0) means in this context, and why every proportional relationship passes through it
If graph paper isn't available, describing points in words/a table works just as well for this lesson's goal
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. The point (3,12) means 3 notebooks cost $12. 2. The point (1,4) means 1 notebook costs $4 — the unit rate. 3. The point (0,0) means 0 notebooks cost $0.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core 7.RP.2d: explaining what a point (x,y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation.
